This page fits into daily work by showing how to handle live-animal bookings with care, consistency, and calm judgment. Companion Animal Travel Desk: animal travel checks and why they matter. I am sorry this can feel detail-heavy at first, but the basics protect the pet, the traveler, and the aircraft. When a booking comes in, listen closely, confirm the species and container details, and keep your tone steady. Safety takes priority over speed in every journey, so do not rush past a welfare concern just to finish the file.

For a rabbit booking, start with the crate fit and ventilation, then compare the container to the carrier rules before you promise acceptance. <<FACT F070>> After that, note any special handling needs and pass unclear cases to the senior coordinator instead of guessing. If the crate seems cramped, damaged, or oddly secured, pause the process and ask for a check.

For bird travel, the weight check is just as important as the paperwork. <<FACT F065>> If the total is out of range, explain that the booking cannot move forward yet and guide the traveler toward a safer solution. Keep your wording simple and humane, because people are often anxious when a pet is involved. The welfare coordinator reviews animal comfort needs, and you should make sure that review has all the facts it needs, including crate condition, feeding notes, and any behavior concerns. If the issue is still not clear after the first review, escalate in the usual calm stepwise way rather than debating at the counter.

Remember to stay patient, document carefully, and put animal welfare first.
